headline: Hormuz shock and Treasury tantrum usher in a decade of financial repression

events: Iran-Gulf naval clashes partially close the Strait of Hormuz for six weeks; Brent spikes to $135 and LNG prices triple in Europe and Asia
French OAT-Bund spread blows out past 200bp after a budget collapses; ECB activates TPI amid German legal challenges
Record heatwave and failed monsoon in South Asia push food inflation above 15% in Pakistan and Bangladesh
Egypt and Kenya miss Eurobond payments; IMF lending capacity visibly stretched after aid cuts
Fed pauses cuts as G20 headline inflation climbs back to ~6%
US 10-year yield breaches 6.5% after a failed 30-year auction during a contested election-year debt-ceiling standoff; Fed launches 'temporary' Treasury purchases
US-China tariff war escalates to semiconductors, rare earths and pharmaceuticals; China imposes graphite and gallium export bans
Bursting of the AI-capex bubble wipes ~30% off big-tech valuations; data-centre buildouts are halved
Category-5 hurricane hits the Texas Gulf Coast, knocking out ~15% of US refining for months
G20 inflation peaks at 7.4%; mass cost-of-living protests across Latin America, Nigeria and southern Europe
Synchronised global recession: world growth slows to 0.6%, global unemployment peaks at 6.5%
UK, Italy and Japan adopt explicit yield caps and bank holding requirements for government bonds; financial repression becomes the norm
Chinese 'customs quarantine' of Taiwan lasts 40 days, triggering emergency chip rationing and Western secondary sanctions
Sovereign defaults or restructurings in Argentina, Pakistan, Ethiopia, Ghana (again) and Bolivia
Firms cut costs by accelerating AI automation of back-office, call-centre and junior professional work
Tepid recovery led by defence spending, grid build-out and energy-security investment; renewables and storage surge as oil-import insurance
Fragile Ukraine ceasefire freezes the front line; Europe commits 3.5% of GDP to defence financed partly by joint EU bonds
Sahel-to-Horn drought and Sudan war spillover drive record migration toward the Mediterranean; far-right gains in three EU governments
AI-driven layoffs in services become a political flashpoint; several US states pass automation taxes
Real interest rates held negative as inflation hovers near 4%, quietly eroding debt ratios but savings too
Second Gulf flare-up briefly spikes oil to $110 but strategic reserves and EV fleets blunt the impact
US public debt reaches ~139% of GDP; interest costs exceed defence spending; bipartisan fiscal commission deadlocks
Two-bloc trade system solidifies with a non-aligned 'swing' group (India, Gulf, ASEAN, Brazil) brokering between them
Global warming passes ~1.6C on a decadal-trend basis after record El Nino-boosted years
Youth unemployment above 20% in much of Africa, South Asia and southern Europe fuels recurring street mobilisations

winners: Gulf states and swing economies (India, Vietnam, Mexico, Gulf) arbitraging between blocs
Defence, grid, battery and energy-security industries
Owners of real assets and land as negative real rates erode cash and bonds
losers: Fixed-income savers and pensioners in advanced economies facing financial repression
Low-income import-dependent countries in Africa and South Asia hit by food, fuel and debt shocks
Young urban renters and entry-level white-collar workers squeezed by housing costs and AI automation
bullets: Debt is managed by inflation and repression rather than austerity: yield caps, bank bond mandates and negative real rates are standard in the US, UK, Japan and much of Europe
Global public debt has climbed to ~109% of GDP, with the US near 139%; nine sovereign debt crises hit mostly frontier and lower-middle-income economies
Growth averaged only ~2% over 2027-31, with a synchronised recession in 2029 and a weak, investment-led recovery
Trade is split into US- and China-led blocs with a pivotal non-aligned middle; chip and critical-mineral supply chains are duplicated at high cost
Energy shocks paradoxically accelerated clean power: renewables reach ~41% of electricity as countries treat solar, wind and storage as security assets
AI adoption reached ~30% of firms after the capex bust, used mainly as a cost-cutting tool in recession, displacing ~50 million jobs and widening inequality
Trust in institutions has sunk to ~28/100; unrest is chronic, with populist and nationalist parties in power or coalitions across many democracies
Climate disasters are now a routine fiscal line item, with hurricanes, heatwaves and droughts repeatedly triggering emergency borrowing
wildcard: A 40-day Chinese 'customs quarantine' of Taiwan in 2029 that ended without shots fired but triggered global chip rationing
image_description: On a sweltering 2031 evening in Milan, a delivery rider waits under a solar-panelled bus shelter while a wall screen flashes a government notice raising the bread subsidy and a riot-police van idles beside a shuttered bank branch.
